buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE 25% : The buyer can increase or decrease the contract quantity or contract duration up to 25 percent at the time of issue of the contract. However, once the contract is issued, the contract quantity or contract duration can only be increased up to 25 percent. Bidders are bound to accept the revised quantity or duration. For lumpsum-based service contracts, the buyer may increase the scope of work and contract value up to 25 percent with the consent of the service provider 2. Generic 1. The Seller shall not assign the Contract in whole or part without obtaining the prior written consent of buyer. 2. The Seller shall not sub-contract the Contract in whole or part to any entity without obtaining the prior written consent of buyer. 3. The Seller shall, notwithstanding the consent and assignment/sub-contract, remain jointly and severally liable and responsible to buyer together with the assignee/ sub-contractor, for and in respect of the due performance of the Contract and the Sellers obligations there under. 3. Service & Support AVAILABILITY OF OFFICE OF SERVICE PROVIDER: An office of the Service Provider must be located in the state of Consignee. DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE TO BE SUBMITTED.

4. Certificates Bidder's offer is liable to be rejected if they don't upload any of the certificates / documents sought in the Bid document, ATC and Corrigendum if any. 5. Buyer Added Bid Specific Scope Of Work(SOW) Text Clause(s) DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES OF SECURITY PERSONNEL l. SECURITY SUPERVISOR

a) Security Supervisor is the representative of Security Contractor available full time in the campus and he is the immediate link between the Security Contractor and the institute's administration. He coordinates and supervises the entire security and fire management arra ngements in the campus in general on behalf of the Security Contractor. b) He will be custodian of all keys of all office rooms in the campus and all registers, documen ts and records of security related activities. c) He will report to the Security Officer of the institute and will be coordinating with the Securi ty Contractor. d) He is responsible for day-to-day boarding of security guards on respective shifts and maint aining the records, attendance registers, visitors registers, and all other documents related t o security arrangements in the campus and at Vanika. e) He will inspect the entire active areas of the campus atleast twice in a shift and will inspec t the entire boundary wall of the campus atlreast once in a week. f) He will ensure that the guards are moving from one place to another for checking the move ment of outsiders and other activities in a well coordinated manner. He will make sure that t he guards are vigilant and moving around atleast in a 100 metre periphery. g) He will carry out drills of guards periodically to ensure their physical fitness and for action t o be taken on unforeseen emergent situation; viz., breach of security and in the event of bre ak out of fire. h) He will organize mock firefighting drills and carry out emergency drills periodically to ensur e readiness in case of fire incidents or breaches of safety. i) He will liaise with the local authorities like police, Municipal Corporation, Hospital, BMC Fire Brigade etc. in case of any need and at other emergencies with information to Security Office r. j) Periodically inspect fire extinguishers and fire safety equipment to ensure they are fully ch arged, unexpired and accessible. k) He will maintain necessary registers related to positing of security guards and day to day i ncidences. These registers should be preserved by him and be produced as and when requir ed. l) As a retired JCO, he ensures all provisions of National Flag Rule and supervise hoisting of N ational Flag and all matters related to it. 2. SECURITY GUARDS Generally, all security guards are required to be alert and vigil with regard to movement of men and anim als in the campus. They should also be vigilant and alert with regard to fire break outs and well trained to put out fires. Apart from this, the point-wise duties and responsibilities are as follows a) Guards at Main Gate • Opening and closing of main gate for employees and visitors. • Making entries in the register of visitors. • Making entries in the register of student movement by properly checking identity cards • Guests visiting the institute need to be guided properly and respectfully to their respective des tinations. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. b) Guard at the Main Building • Ensure proper parking of vehicles. • Patrolling from visitors vehicle parking area to end of employees car parking area. • To be vigilant around the Horticulture Nursery area. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. c) Guard in the Main Building/ Key Handler • Opening and closing of all rooms in the main building as per laid down procedures. • Putting on and putting off all lights in the corridors.

• To be alert and vigilant inside the main building. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. d) Guard at the Boys Hostel • Security and vigilance in the Boys Hostel and surrounding areas. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. e) Lady Guard in the Girls Hostels • Security and vigilance in the Girls Hostel and surrounding areas. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. f) Guard at the Director's Bungalow Security and vigilance in the Director's bungalow and the surrounding areas including Guest House. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. g) Guards on Patrolling • Patrolling around the campus, as guided by the Supervisor from time to time. • Reporting of conditions and status of the boundary wall to the supervisor. • Reporting of the status of street lights in the campus. • Maintain constant vigilance across all areas of the campus to prevent and instantly detect fire hazards or outbreaks. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. h) Guards at Vanika Residential Colony • Maintaining the entries of visitors to the colony in the given register. • Taking the stock of boundary wall and reporting the conditions to Supervisor. • Checking the functioning of street lights in Vanika. • Maintain constant vigilance across all areas of the colony to prevent and instantly detect fire h azards or outbreaks. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. i) Guard at Auditorium • Monitor and manage the entry and exit of students, faculty, staff, and official visitors during ev ents, seminars, conferences, and daily academic activities. • Security and vigilance in the Auditorium and surrounding areas. • Keep a strict watch on fire safety compliance inside the auditorium. • Open and securely lock the auditorium doors. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. 15. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses ADDITIONAL GENERAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS (ATC) 01. ELIGIBILITY & ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS FOR EVALUATION:

1. The bidder should have valid Registration Licence under M.P. Shops & Establishment Act and have alr eady existing functional office at Bhopal (M.P.) prior to creation of bid. 2. The bidder should submit an affidavit (₹100 non-judicial stamp paper) stating that they have never b een black listed / debarred from any Central/State Govt. establishment for the similar work of Security & Fire Management Services. 3. The Bidder must submit one copy each of the following license/ certificates in GeM portal. The Origin al may be submitted for verification and the same will be returned to the bidder after due verification: a) PSARA License b) Labour License c) License under PF, EPF Code & Misc. Provisions Act d) License issued under M.P. Shops & Establishment Act e) Affidavit (₹100 non-judicial stamp paper) stating that they have never been black listed / deb arred f) ESIC Act Certificate g) GST Certificate h) PAN Number i) Turnover Certificate, if applicable 4. A prospective bidder, requiring any clarification on the Bid Documents shall notify the Purchaser in w riting by Post or by Email of the Purchaser as indicated in the invitation of Bid. The Purchaser shall res pond in writing to any request for the clarification of the Bid Documents, which it receives 07 days pri or to the date of opening of the Tenders. Copies of the query (without identifying the source) and clari fications by the Purchaser shall be sent to all the prospective bidders who have received the bid docu ments. 5. Any clarification issued by IIFM, Bhopal in response to query raised by prospective bidders shall form an integral part of bid documents and shall amount to an amendment of the relevant clauses of the bi d documents. 02. AMENDMENT OF BID DOCUMENTS 1. The Buyer may, for any reason, whether at its own initiative or in response to a clarification requeste d by a prospective bidder, may modify bid documents by amendments prior to the date of submissio n of Bids. The amendments shall be notified through the e-tendering portal and these amendments wi ll be binding on all the bidders. 2. In order to afford prospective bidders a reasonable time to take the amendment into account in prep aring their bids, the purchaser may, at its discretion, extend the deadline for the submission of bids s uitably. 03. SUPPLY OF MANPOWER: 1. The Institute (IIFM, Bhopal), at present, has requirement of workload equivalent to 03 male (ESM S ecurity Supervisor in Skilled category above subedar rank with qualification of secondary school) + 6 male (unarmed ESM security guard in semi-skilled category with qualification of high school) as w ell as 24 Male (unarmed security guard in semi-skilled category with qualification of high school) a nd 9 female (unarmed security guard in semi-skilled category with qualification of high school). The requirement of this Institute may further increase or decrease during the period of contract and the contractor would have to increase or decrease the manpower supply, if required on the same terms and conditions. 2. The Service Provider shall ensure that manpower deployed in the Indian Institute of Forest Manage ment, Bhopal (IIFM Bhopal), are competent enough to carry out the work. 3. IIFM reserves the right to increase or decrease up to 25% of the quantity of goods or services specified in the schedule of requirements without any change in the unit price or other terms and con ditions at the time of award of contract. 04. DEPLOYMENT & OPERATION OF SECURITY MANPOWER

1. The selection of security personnel to be deployed at the IIFM main Campus and the Vanika Residential colony must be done in consultation with/ approval of the Institute. 2. That the agency is required to install a biometric attendance machine at The Bidder own cost for recor ding the attendance of the manpower deployed at the IIFM main campus and the Vanika Residential co lony, and the record of this attendance will be the basis for payment of wages. LAN Networking connec tion used for biometric attendance machine will be provided by IIFM. 3. That the agency will have to take over the charge of security and fire management services physicall y from the existing agency along with all assets, property, building (keys) in the presence of IIFM's Sec urity Officer. 4. That the details of assets will be handed over to the Bidder separately. 5. That the bidder is required to submit the contact details (Name, Designation and Mobile No.) of the p erson (and an alternate person) who will be responsible for overall management of the security and fir e management services at IIFM. 6. The Contractor has to deploy and work during holidays, late hours and Sundays as well according to t he requirement and convenience of IIFM and the occupants, while ensuring weekly offs of his / her emp loyees as per statutory requirements. 05. PERIOD OF CONTRACT & EXTENSION 1. The contract shall automatically expire after ONE (01) year from the commencement of the contrac t unless extended further by the mutual consent of Institute and contracting agency/firm. If the contra ctor services are found satisfactory during the contract period, this contract may be extended, year t o year basis on the same terms and conditions or with some modification, for a further period not exc eeding two (02) years in total. The approved agency/contractor will have to apply in writing for such e xtensions well in advance before the expiry date of contract. The agency/contractor will have no clai m for such extensions neither this will be binding on him to accept such extensions offered by IIFM, B hopal. 2. If the services provided are not found satisfactory during the period, then the competent authority c an terminate the order by giving one-month prior notice on the sole discretion / decision of IIFM, Bhop al. 06. CONDUCT & MISCONDUCT 1. That the agency shall ensure that its personnel shall not be found consuming Pan Masala, Gutka or Sm oking or taking any prohibited psychotropic drugs or alcohol in the IIFM premises and at Vanika or indu lging in any such activities during the working hours. 2. That the agency shall ensure that the security or other personnel, deployed at IIFM and at Vanika be d ressed and groomed appropriately while on the premises of IIFM campus and Vanika. Further, they will perform and discharge their duties with the highest degree of professionalism and dedication to the be st of their abilities. 3. That the agency shall ensure at all times, the maintenance of the confidentiality in the performance of security personnel's official duties as required by the professional standard and ethics, particularly wit h regard to information, disclosure of which may prejudicially affect the interest or security of the Instit ute. 4. That in case of theft/ robbery (includes any attempt or abetment thereof) or any physical damage to t he Institute's property occurs by any act or omission or lapses on the part of The Bidder security perso nnel, the losses so caused will be recovered will be set off against any payment due towards IIFM. 5. That the agency shall ensure that the security personnel be prohibited from photographing, video-gra phing or recording any image in any medium in the IIFM campus or in the premises of the Vanika with out the permission of the competent authorities. 6. That the agency shall ensure that the security personnel deployed at the institute must behave in a co urteous, polite, and proper manner with students, staff, faculty, employees, and visitors at all times. 7. The security agency must provide periodic orientation programs to security guards to enhance their so ft skills, communication, and overall effectiveness in executing their duties. 07. PAYMENT 1. That the monthly bills pertaining to each month must be submitted before 11th day of the following m

onth along with an undertaking (on ₹50/- non-judicial stamp paper with notary) regarding disbursal of f ull payment to the deployed security towards their wages paid by the IIFM. The declaration showing pa yment of above-mentioned monthly wages to the individual security personnel against their specific b ank account numbers and the payment after first month shall be released only when the following essential documents pertaining to the previous months are submitted along with the respective bills: a. Declaration showing payment of monthly wages to the individual employees against their spe cific bank account numbers. b. Declaration showing payment of EPF contributions towards the individual employees with cop y of the EPF account statement of individual security personnel duly signed by the concerned person. c. Declaration showing payment of ESI contributions towards the individual employees with a co py of the ESI payment challan. d. Copy of the Service Tax payment challan exclusively against the payment made by the Institu te along with quarterly service tax return certificate, if any. 2. That the agency shall, at all times, comply with all the applicable laws, statutes, regulations, and code s relating to payment of wages, and further ensure that the exact number of wages charged to the IIF M be released by to its security or other personnel, deployed in the service of IIFM. Any failure to comp ly with the provisions contained herein can lead to termination of the contract. 3. The agency shall not charge any money/fees/deductions in whatever manner, name, or form, or take a ny monetary/ non-monetary considerations, or make any unlawful deductions from the compensation/ salary of the manpower/ employees/ resources engaged by it and, to be deployed at IIFM and Vanika R esidential Colony. 4. The Agency/Service Provider shall not indulge in any unethical practices. 08. PENALTY: 1. The Service Provider shall immediately provide a substitute in the event of any person leaving the j ob due to his / her personal reasons. The delay by the Service Provider in providing a substitute be yond two working days shall attract liquidated damages @ Rs. 500/- per day (per such case) on the service-providing Firm/agency, besides deduction in payment on pro-rata basis. 2. The contractor shall indemnify IIFM Bhopal against payments to be made under and for the observan ce of the laws. 3. IIFM Bhopal shall have the right to deduct from the money due to the contractor any sum required or estimated to be required, for making good the loss suffered by a worker or workers, by reasons of non - fulfilment of the conditions of the contract of the benefit of the workers, non- payment of wages or of deduction made from his/her or their wages which are not justified by their terms of the contract or n on- observance of the Regulations. The event of any failure in this regard and in the event of any loss/ damages caused directly or indirectly to IIFM Bhopal, the same shall be payable by the contractor alo ng with such penalty as may be decided by the Institute which shall not be less than 10% of the total l oss suffered by the IIFM Bhopal. 4. In case, the tendering Service Provider fails to comply with the statutory/ taxation liability under appro priate law, and as a result thereof IIFM Bhopal is put to any loss/obligation, monetary or otherwise, IIFM Bhopal will be entitled to get itself reimbursed out of the outstanding bills or the Performance Security Deposit of the Service Provider, to the extent of the loss or obligation in monitory terms. 5. If excess payment is made due to any reason/mistake, the party has to refund it immediately otherwis e it may be adjusted against any pending bills or security deposits. 6. The deduction can be imposed by the buyer for the delay of payments of wages by the Service Provide r and deposit of EPF & ESIC (Both employee & employer share) as per Special Terms and Conditions (S TC) prescribed in the GeM contract. 09.TERMINATION OF CONTRACT: 1. The contractor shall be bound by the details furnished by him/ her to this office, while submitting the bid/tender or at subsequent stage. In case, any of such documents furnished by him/ her is found to b e false at any stage, it would be deemed to be a breach of terms of contract making him/ her liable for legal action besides termination of contract. 2. In case of breach of any of terms and conditions mentioned in this bid/tender, the IIFM Bhopal will hav e the right to cancel the work order without assigning any reason thereof and nothing will be payable by the Institute in that event and the security deposit shall also stand forfeited. 3. This Institute reserves right to terminate the contract giving a week’s notice to the contracting Serv ice Provider. 4. This Institute reserves right to terminate the contract and the firm/Service Provider will be black listed, if any mal practice or violating any applicable laws is reported. 5. The IIFM Bhopal may at any time terminate the contract by giving written notice to the Contractor, wit hout compensation to the contractor, if the Contractor becomes bankrupt or otherwise insolvent as de

clared by the competent court provided that such termination will not prejudice or affect any right or a ction or remedy which has accrued or will accrue thereafter to IIFM Bhopal. 6. The Institute may at any time, at its option cancel and terminate this contract by written notice to th e contractor short close the tender/bid without any compensation to the contractor. Contractor shall b e paid for the work, which has been actually completed upto the date of such action by IIFM Bhopal. 7. That, in addition to this work order, the scope of services, rules and responsibilities, any additional r esponsibility, agency obligations, penalties and termination conditions will be applicable as contain ed in the above referred GeM contract. 10. PERFORMANCE SECURITY GUARANTEE 1. Within 28 days of receipt of the Letter of Acceptance/ Award of Contract, the successful Bidder shall d eliver to the CAO a Performance Security Deposit of Amount 5% of the annual contract amount, payabl e to the Director, IIFM, Bhopal in the form of Demand Draft/ Bankers’ Cheque/ FDR/ IMPS/ RTGS/ NEFT/ Bank Guarantee for a validity period of Fourteen Months (14 Months) from the date of commencement of contract, duly discharged and endorsed in favour of Director, IIFM, Bhopal. 2. The successful Bidder shall provide the Performance Security Guarantee as above, which is issued by a Nationalized Indian Bank only. 3. Failure of the successful Bidder to comply with the requirements of any clause of this document shall constitute sufficient grounds for cancellation of the award of work and forfeiture of the Performance Se curity Guarantee, as the case may be. · Beneficiary Name: Director IIFM · IFSC Code: SBIN0012194 · Account No.: 30662291254 · Branch address: IIFM Branch · Bank Name: State Bank of India 11. COMPLIANCE With LAWS 1. The contractor will himself be responsible for all the statutory obligations of the Labour Law, & other Acts etc. IIFM will not be responsible for any violation of the labour laws by the contractor. He shall mai ntain the register regarding statutory obligations of the labour laws and produce the same to the IIFM Authority on demand. 2. The contractor should abide by all labour rules, wages, welfare, EPF, ESI conditions & obligations durin g the contract period. 3. The tenderer must ensure and will be responsible that the staff deployed by him is paid their salary a nd allowances electronically direct to their Bank Accounts latest by 10th of the following month and en sure that the requirements of the Payment of Wages Act, Employees’ Contract labour Act are strictly c omplied with. He should maintain proper records of salaries paid and this should be available for scruti ny of the IIFM Management as and when required. 12. Dispute Resolution 1. In the event of any question, dispute or difference arising out of this agreement or in connection there- with (except as to the matters, the decision to which is specifically provided under this agreement), th e same shall be referred to the sole arbitrator. The arbitrator shall be appointed by the IIFM, Bhopal. 2. The agreement to appoint an arbitrator and proceedings of the arbitration will be in accordance with t he Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 as amended from time to time. 3. a) Security Supervisor is the representative of Security Contractor available full time in the campus and he is the immediate link between the Security Contractor and the institute's administration. He coordinates and supervises the entire security and fire management arra ngements in the campus in general on behalf of the Security Contractor. b) He will be custodian of all keys of all office rooms in the campus and all registers, documen ts and records of security related activities. c) He will report to the Security Officer of the institute and will be coordinating with the Securi ty Contractor. d) He is responsible for day-to-day boarding of security guards on respective shifts and maint aining the records, attendance registers, visitors registers, and all other documents related t o security arrangements in the campus and at Vanika. e) He will inspect the entire active areas of the campus atleast twice in a shift and will inspec t the entire boundary wall of the campus atlreast once in a week. f) He will ensure that the guards are moving from one place to another for checking the move ment of outsiders and other activities in a well coordinated manner. He will make sure that t he guards are vigilant and moving around atleast in a 100 metre periphery. g) He will carry out drills of guards periodically to ensure their physical fitness and for action t o be taken on unforeseen emergent situation; viz., breach of security and in the event of bre ak out of fire. h) He will organize mock firefighting drills and carry out emergency drills periodically to ensur e readiness in case of fire incidents or breaches of safety. i) He will liaise with the local authorities like police, Municipal Corporation, Hospital, BMC Fire Brigade etc. in case of any need and at other emergencies with information to Security Office r. j) Periodically inspect fire extinguishers and fire safety equipment to ensure they are fully ch arged, unexpired and accessible. k) He will maintain necessary registers related to positing of security guards and day to day i ncidences. These registers should be preserved by him and be produced as and when requir ed. l) As a retired JCO, he ensures all provisions of National Flag Rule and supervise hoisting of N ational Flag and all matters related to it. 2. SECURITY GUARDS Generally, all security guards are required to be alert and vigil with regard to movement of men and anim als in the campus. They should also be vigilant and alert with regard to fire break outs and well trained to put out fires. Apart from this, the point-wise duties and responsibilities are as follows a) Guards at Main Gate • Opening and closing of main gate for employees and visitors. • Making entries in the register of visitors. • Making entries in the register of student movement by properly checking identity cards • Guests visiting the institute need to be guided properly and respectfully to their respective des tinations. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. b) Guard at the Main Building • Ensure proper parking of vehicles. • Patrolling from visitors vehicle parking area to end of employees car parking area. • To be vigilant around the Horticulture Nursery area. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. c) Guard in the Main Building/ Key Handler • Opening and closing of all rooms in the main building as per laid down procedures. • Putting on and putting off all lights in the corridors.

• To be alert and vigilant inside the main building. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. d) Guard at the Boys Hostel • Security and vigilance in the Boys Hostel and surrounding areas. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. e) Lady Guard in the Girls Hostels • Security and vigilance in the Girls Hostel and surrounding areas. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. f) Guard at the Director's Bungalow Security and vigilance in the Director's bungalow and the surrounding areas including Guest House. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. g) Guards on Patrolling • Patrolling around the campus, as guided by the Supervisor from time to time. • Reporting of conditions and status of the boundary wall to the supervisor. • Reporting of the status of street lights in the campus. • Maintain constant vigilance across all areas of the campus to prevent and instantly detect fire hazards or outbreaks. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. h) Guards at Vanika Residential Colony • Maintaining the entries of visitors to the colony in the given register. • Taking the stock of boundary wall and reporting the conditions to Supervisor. • Checking the functioning of street lights in Vanika. • Maintain constant vigilance across all areas of the colony to prevent and instantly detect fire h azards or outbreaks. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. i) Guard at Auditorium • Monitor and manage the entry and exit of students, faculty, staff, and official visitors during ev ents, seminars, conferences, and daily academic activities. • Security and vigilance in the Auditorium and surrounding areas. • Keep a strict watch on fire safety compliance inside the auditorium. • Open and securely lock the auditorium doors. • Any other work assigned to them by the Security Supervisor. 15.
